question: Same list as data-fresh-universe-v1, with the failed downloads retried and their reasons recorded, and the $5 floor judged on the unadjusted close (v1 judged the split-adjusted close, which drops the early years of stocks that later split). Engineering check: lists and counts only, no returns.
next_step: Each v2 shard becomes a frozen dataset (daily history from 1995, keeping the unadjusted close) registered separately; the frozen weekly V3 pattern is tested on these unseen stocks.
notes: data-fresh-universe-v1 did not pass its own criterion: 3,352 of 21,499 downloads failed (15.6% > 10%); it kept 5,743 stocks. The result stays as recorded.

Version 2: the same candidates; downloads use five attempts with three parallel requests, and every failure gets one more slow pass. A failure is either 'empty' (the provider has no history for that code, mostly delisted '_old' codes: a survivorship gap that is reported, not hidden) or an error (HTTP or timeout).
Passed if errors after the retry are at most 2% of candidates and at least 1,000 stocks are kept; empty histories are reported separately.
The $5 floor uses the provider's unadjusted close; the $10M floor uses the adjusted close times the provider's split-adjusted volume, as in v1.
Tickers the provider marks as reused carry suffixes (_old, _old1, a trailing digit), so no ticker joins two companies.
